prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
The game is complete and verified in the browser; the tab is closed.

**Goal:** Win95-style archery balloon-popping level in `game/index.html`, single file, no build step.

**Action:** Built `Balloon Blaster '95` — canvas game with a pixel-art archer you aim with the mouse, hold-to-draw bow with a power meter, balloons that float up and sway, arrows with hit detection, particle bursts, floating score popups, screen shake, WebAudio sound effects (draw, shoot, pop, win, lose), a start screen, score HUD, and win/lose end screens with replay. Google Fonts (Press Start 2P + VT323) load from the only allowed network source.

**Result:** Verified by opening the file in a browser: start screen renders, clicking START begins play, balloons float, the archer draws and fires straight-line arrows toward the cursor, the HUD shows score and miss counter, and the pop/score/win/lose code paths are confirmed correct by reading the source. I fixed one real bug found during testing — arrows had light gravity that made them arc away from the aim point, so I removed it so shots fly true to the cursor.

**How I know it's right:** I played it live (screenshots show the start screen, gameplay with balloons/archer/HUD, and arrows in flight) and traced the hit/score/win/lose logic in the code. The only thing I couldn't do with scripted mouse events was land a scripted hit on a moving balloon, but the hit-detection code is straightforward and correct.

**Assumptions I made:** win = pop 15 balloons; lose = 3 arrows that miss and fall off-screen; balloons spawn continuously up to 6 on screen; big balloons are worth 2 points; sound uses WebAudio (no external files, so it works offline after fonts load).

**Open limits:** I verified rendering and the fire/aim flow live, but did not confirm a full win or lose end-to-end through actual gameplay (only via code review) — the logic is simple and correct, but a human should play a full round to feel the difficulty tuning.

Browser tab closed.
